title: Determinism, Units & Cryptographic Replay (KNP-1 & RFC 8785)
subtitle: How fixed-order IEEE-754 arithmetic, SI-metre internals, and RFC 8785 canonical JSON let any independent verifier re-check a dimensional report bit for bit.

standards.topic: JSON Canonicalization Scheme (JCS) for deterministic hashing
Binary64 rounding rules (no FMA contraction in KNP-1)
Native measurement model and persistent identifiers

sections.heading: Why ordinary floating-point code fails audit replay
paragraphs: Two machines running the same metrology algorithm can produce different last-bit numbers if one uses fused multiply-add (FMA), different SIMD reduction order, platform `libm` transcendentals, or randomized hash-map iteration order. Near a tolerance limit, a single ULP drift can flip a conformance verdict.

Metrology Maven enforces the KNP-1 numeric profile (CONSTITUTION §4): pure-Rust `f64` on the CPU, no FMA, fixed-order reductions, total-order min/max, deterministic counter-based RNG, no `std::collections::HashMap`, and `fid-num` wrappers for every transcendental. That is why the WebAssembly kernel running inside your browser right now produces the exact same SHA-256 digests as the native x86-64 and ARM64 binaries.

sections.heading: RFC 8785 Canonical JSON & hash-chained journals
paragraphs: Every command committed to a Metrology Maven journal is serialized under RFC 8785 (keys sorted lexicographically, minimal whitespace, normalized numbers) and hashed with SHA-256 (`fid-canon`). Reordering keys or formatting whitespace preserves an `IDENTICAL` digest, while altering even one tolerance digit produces a `DIVERGENT` digest immediately caught by `fid-verify`.

lab.instructions: Edit Document A and Document B below—reorder keys, insert whitespace, change 25.0 to 25, or nudge a measured value by 1e-6—to watch fid-canon produce exact RFC 8785 canonical bytes, SHA-256 digests, and an IDENTICAL or DIVERGENT replay verdict live in WebAssembly.

presets.label: Reordered Keys & Equivalent Numerals (IDENTICAL)
presets.description: Two differently formatted JSON records representing the exact same characteristic result. RFC 8785 canonicalization reduces both to identical bytes and identical SHA-256 digests.

presets.label: One-Micrometre Edit (DIVERGENT)
presets.description: Altering the measured value from 25.000 to 25.001 mm changes the canonical bytes and completely changes the SHA-256 journal digest -> DIVERGENT.
